name: Myrtle Avenue
tagline: The classic — westerly arrivals about 150 ft over the fence
access: Piccadilly line to Hatton Cross, then roughly a 10-minute walk: south down Hatton Road from the Great South West Road (A30), then right into Myrtle Avenue. The viewing area is the rough grass at the top of the road, by the airport fence. Street parking only, and the residents need it.
notes: You stand about 450 m short of the 27L threshold and 100 m south of the centreline, so arrivals pass low and slightly to your right — a wide lens is enough for an A380. Because you are looking east up the approach, the light is best from early afternoon onwards; it turns to mud after rain and there is no shelter or anywhere to sit.
transport: Hatton Cross (Piccadilly line), about 10 minutes on foot

name: Hatton Cross & Southern Perimeter Road
tagline: Touchdown zone views straight off the Tube
access: Hatton Cross station and bus station sit right on the Great South West Road. Leave by the bus station and follow the footway west along the Southern Perimeter Road for three to five minutes to reach the fence.
notes: Arrivals cross the fence roughly 600 m short of the 27L threshold at about 150 ft and touch down away to your west, so this is a spot for landing rolls and reverser shots more than head-on approach shots. It is a working perimeter road with constant traffic and no shelter, but it is the easiest place at Heathrow to reach, and to leave when the weather turns.
transport: Hatton Cross (Piccadilly line) and Hatton Cross bus station
facilities: Shops and takeaways at the station; nothing at the fence itself

name: Eastern Perimeter Road
tagline: 27R short final at the fence, around 170 ft up
access: Walk north from Hatton Cross along the Eastern Perimeter Road, about 20 to 25 minutes, or come in from the north from a Bath Road bus stop at Cranford. There is no continuous footway, so you will be on the verge in places.
notes: About 700 m short of the 27R threshold and 170 m south of the centreline, which puts westerly arrivals overhead at roughly 170 ft. There is only a narrow strip of verge to stand on, the road carries cargo traffic all day, and airport security drives past often enough that you should expect to be asked what you are doing.
transport: Hatton Cross (Piccadilly line), then a 20-25 minute walk north

name: Waye Avenue Park, Cranford
tagline: Open grass under the eastern approach, well away from the fence
access: Waye Avenue is a residential street in Cranford, north of the Great South West Road; the park, playground and allotments are at its southern end. Bath Road (A4) bus routes serve Cranford, and Hounslow West on the Piccadilly line is about 25 minutes' walk east. Park considerately — this is somebody's street.
notes: You are 1.4 km out from the 27R threshold and about 220 m south of the centreline, so arrivals cross at roughly 300 ft and off to your left; 200 mm or more if you want them tight. It is open, grassy and much calmer than the perimeter roads, and under easterly operations the departure climb-out passes over the same ground.
transport: Bath Road (A4) buses to Cranford; Hounslow West (Piccadilly line) about 25 minutes' walk
facilities: Open grass and a playground; no toilets or refreshments

name: Northern Perimeter Road (Renaissance)
tagline: Touchdowns and rollouts from the north side
access: Bath Road bus stops by the Renaissance hotel put you a few minutes from the grass strips along the Northern Perimeter Road, between the car park decks. Driving here means finding somewhere legal to leave the car, which is the hard part.
notes: You are roughly 800 m past the 27R threshold and 220 m north of the centreline, so westerly arrivals touch down in front of you and roll past — good for reversers and rollout, not for approach shots. Being on the north side it is into the light for most of the day and only really comes good late in the afternoon; floodlight poles are in the way whatever you do.
transport: Bath Road bus stops (Renaissance hotel); nearest rail is Heathrow Terminals 2 & 3
facilities: Bath Road hotels for food and toilets

name: Northern Perimeter Road — 27R Line-Up
tagline: Whales lining up and rolling, 200 m from the fence
access: The eastern end of the Northern Perimeter Road, reached from Bath Road on foot or by local bus towards the cargo area. It is a short walk from the Renaissance stretch of the same road.
notes: This sits almost abeam the 27R threshold and about 190 m north of the centreline, so under westerly operations departures hold, line up and start their roll directly in front of you. Summer evenings are the time to be here; there is nowhere to sit and nothing to stand on, and the noise on the roll is serious.
transport: Bath Road bus stops; nearest rail is Heathrow Terminals 2 & 3

name: Heathrow Academy Viewing Stand
tagline: The only official free viewing area for non-passengers
access: Newall Road, TW6 2RQ, off the Northern Perimeter Road. Local buses serve Bath Road a few minutes away; the nearest rail station is Heathrow Terminals 2 & 3. The stand itself is free at all times, but the car park is charged.
notes: A covered stand looking south across the northern runway, so it works in rain and it is the one place at Heathrow where you are actually meant to be standing. You are about 300 m back from the runway with fencing and light poles in between, so it is much better for watching and logging than for tight photography.
transport: Bath Road buses; Heathrow Terminals 2 & 3 (Piccadilly and Elizabeth lines)

name: Terminal 5 — 09L Approach Embankment
tagline: Easterly arrivals about 150 ft overhead, a walk from T5
access: From Terminal 5 arrivals, follow the footway north along Wallis Road past the security post to the Western Perimeter Road; the grass embankment and its narrow paths are on the far side. Allow about 15 minutes on foot.
notes: Only worth the walk under easterly operations, when 09L arrivals cross the embankment about 575 m from the threshold at roughly 150 ft, with the morning sun behind you as you look west. Under westerlies the 27R departures climb out over the same ground. The bank is steep, unlit and completely bare — bring what you need.

name: Western Perimeter Road
tagline: Almost exactly under the 09R approach and 27L climb-out
access: About 15 minutes' walk south from Terminal 5 along the Western Perimeter Road. Driving means using the lay-bys, and there is no official parking anywhere near.
notes: The centreline of the southern runway runs within 30 m of this point, so 09R arrivals cross about 670 m from the threshold at roughly 160 ft, and under westerlies 27L departures climb straight over your head. It is a fast road with a narrow verge and no shelter, and the noise at close range is genuinely punishing.

name: Stanwell Moor & King George VI Reservoir
tagline: Westerly departures overhead, with a pub garden underneath
access: Horton Road, Stanwell Moor (TW19 6AQ). The 442 bus from Terminal 5 towards Staines stops in the village; on foot it is roughly 35 minutes from T5. Street parking only, so leave room for residents.
notes: Under westerly operations 27L departures cross the village at one to two thousand feet, already turning; under easterlies 09R arrivals pass about 1.4 km from the threshold at roughly 300 ft, a couple of hundred metres to the north. The Anchor's beer garden on Horton Road is the comfortable option. The footpaths towards King George VI Reservoir get you further under the departure track but are muddy, exposed and unlit, and the reservoir itself is Thames Water land with no public access.
transport: Bus 442 from Heathrow Terminal 5; nearest rail is Terminal 5 (Piccadilly and Elizabeth lines)
facilities: The Anchor pub on Horton Road — food, toilets and a small car park; nothing else in the village

name: View Heathrow, Terminal 4
tagline: Indoor deck over the southern runway — boarding pass required
access: Airside in Terminal 4, near gates 15 and 16, past security. Departing passengers only — there is no landside way in, so this is a spot for the day you are flying, not the day you are spotting.
notes: A glass-fronted deck with a long view north over the southern runway and the Terminal 4 stands, with binoculars and flight-tracking screens provided. Shooting through glass costs you sharpness and the runway is about 700 m away, but it is warm, dry and the only place at Heathrow you can sit down and watch a runway.
facilities: Seating, binoculars and flight-tracking screens; full airside terminal facilities nearby
